anki.title: Anki My
anki.description: A self-hosted flashcard application inspired by Anki, built with React and TypeScript on the frontend and a Rust (Rocket) REST API backend.
anki.summary: Anki My is a web study tool built to explore how a polished frontend can interact with a high-performance Rust backend for state and data management.
anki.problem: Studying with flashcards requires dynamic deck management, stable server-side persistence, and a low-friction interface. The project focuses on creating a secure, self-hosted spaced repetition system.
anki.focus: Rust backend APIs, PostgreSQL database integration (SQLx), JWT authentication, React UI, and a clear separation between frontend and backend services.
features: JWT authentication (register/login) with bcrypt password hashing
Create, update, and manage flashcard decks
Add, edit, and review cards with front/back contents
Browse shared public decks and filter by name
learnings: Structuring a decoupled web application with Rust and React
Implementing secure JWT auth flows and password encryption
Managing relational database connections and migrations with SQLx and PostgreSQL

firstgameengine.title: First Game Engine
firstgameengine.description: A custom game engine experiment built from scratch with C++, OpenGL, GLFW, and GLEW to study rendering, shaders, assets, and engine structure.
firstgameengine.summary: First Game Engine is a low-level C++ project where I explored how rendering systems, shader loading, assets, and engine loops fit together.
firstgameengine.problem: Game engines hide a lot of complexity. Building a small engine from scratch helped me understand the rendering pipeline, application loop, and how different systems need to communicate.
firstgameengine.focus: C++ architecture, OpenGL rendering, shader management, asset rendering, input, and collision-oriented foundations.
features: OpenGL rendering pipeline with VAO, VBO, EBO and shader management
First-person free camera with mouse look and delta-time movement
Scene and entity system with per-entity transform (position, rotation, scale)
Input system with key states (pressed / held / released) and mouse tracking
Abstract Logic interface to decouple game logic from the engine loop
CMake build system with each module compiled as static libraries
learnings: Working closer to graphics APIs and memory constraints
Organizing C++ code for systems that grow over time
Understanding how rendering, input, and update loops interact

petadopt.title: Adote um Pet (NGO Pet Adoption Platform)
petadopt.description: A PHP + MySQL web application that manages the full pet adoption workflow for an animal shelter/NGO: registering rescued animals, publishing them for adoption, and routing adoption requests through a staff approval process.
petadopt.summary: Pet Adoption System is a PHP web application managing user flows, pet profiles, and multi-user adoption workflows with direct database queries and robust session constraints.
petadopt.problem: Shelter management requires coordination between staff and adopters, secure routing, role boundaries, and transactions to prevent concurrent requests for the same pet.
petadopt.focus: Front-controller routing, Table Data Gateway pattern, raw SQL transactions with row-level locks, session-based access guards, and security hardening.
features: Unified routing and output buffering layout template
Table Data Gateway classes abstracting SQL operations
Explicit database transaction flow with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks
Dynamic role-based access control and session verification guards
learnings: Implementing transaction boundaries and row-level locks in relational databases
Designing clean OOP database access using the Table Data Gateway pattern
Enforcing role-aware access controls and secure session management in raw PHP

setup.workflow_desc: To prevent race conditions where multiple adopters request the same animal concurrently, the system uses PDO transactions paired with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row-level locks:
workflow_steps: createRequest(): locks the animal, creates the request, and sets its status to Em_adocao.
approve(): approves one request, cancels the pending ones, and marks the animal as Adotado.
cancel(): cancels the request and returns the animal to Disponivel only when no other active request exists.

setup.limits_desc: Several architectural improvements are suggested to modernize the application codebase:
limits_list: Password Hashing: Currently hashes passwords using MySQL's PASSWORD() function, which is deprecated in modern MySQL 8.x. Recommended: migration to PHP's secure password_hash() / password_verify().
Hardcoded Credentials: DB config is hardcoded in Database.php. Recommended: externalize settings to config.php or environment variables.
Placeholder 404: The 404 page is empty and does not render. The router silently falls back to home.
No CSRF Tokens: POST forms lack security tokens. Recommended: add anti-CSRF token verification.
Photo Storage: Stores photos as binary LONGBLOBs. Recommended: store files on disk or cloud storage and save file paths in the database.

projects.architecture_desc: The engine enforces a clean separation between core systems and application logic through the Core::Logic interface. The game loop in Core::Game calls onUpdate() and onRender() each frame, which the game application implements.
projects.camera_desc: Core::Graphics::Camera computes view and projection matrices, while FreeCam extends it with WASD + QE movement and mouse look controls.
projects.input_desc: Core::Input tracks three key states per key (pressed, held, released) and calculates frame delta time for frame-rate-independent movement.
